| | Peter, We generally remember ancient Rome for its sprawling empire and powerful emperors. But overlooked by our fascination with the might and drama of imperial Rome is the fact that Rome reached its greatness through a far different form of government. Did you know that Caesar Augustus inherited 90% of the territory of his Empire from the Roman Republic? The story of how the Roman Republic emerged from a group of warring tribes in the middle of the Italian peninsula to dominate the Mediterranean and, later, most of Europe is a captivating narrative of achievement, political and military genius, and the perils of success.
---

name: Wes Moore
subject: My proposal to balance the Maryland state budget
body:
Friend,

I just released my proposal to balance the state budget to address Maryland’s budget crisis. Here’s what you should know:

* Nearly two-thirds of Marylanders will get a tax cut.
* We will lower the corporate tax rate and focus on making Maryland more competitive and business-friendly.
* Our plan cuts spending by $2 billion.

This is a bold plan — but the moment requires bold action to ensure we are creating a sustainable budget for the year and investing in our future.

These aren’t easy decisions. The current budget crisis has been in the making for nearly a decade, and we need to create a responsible budget that balances economic growth, and weathering the current crisis at hand.

It is our responsibility to weather the year ahead and emerge stronger. Making the tough decisions now ensures we can maintain our focus on growing the middle class and provide pathways for Marylanders to find good jobs, earn fair wages, and have opportunities to increase wealth. We are going to do that by creating jobs, prioritizing regulatory reform, and making it easier for businesses to grow and stay in Maryland.

We lead through partnership. By working together, we will win this moment and leave no one behind.

Elevate,

Wes

Dear friends,
In times of crisis, the truth is more than ever. And unfortunately, social media makes it possible for lies to spread quicker than the speed of light.
Here are some fact-checks to set the record straight. And you can always get up-to-date information from CaliforniaFireFacts.com [CaliforniaFireFacts.com] :
##
CLAIM: California has cut the fire budget and personnel in recent years.
FACT: The number of CalFIRE staff and the CalFIRE budget have nearly doubled since Gov. Newsom took office.
##
CLAIM: These wildfires are caused by California’s mismanagement of forest lands.
FACT: The budget for forest management is TEN TIMES larger than it was in 2018, and we have more than doubled the number of acres treated for wildfire resilience. Also, not all of the current fires even started in forested areas.
##
CLAIM: California’s reservoirs are empty because all the water is "emptied out into the ocean.”
FACT: Water reservoirs in Southern California are at record levels. There is no shortage of water in Southern California. PolitiFact independently found [https://www.politifact.com/article/2025/jan/10/fact-check-los-angeles-fires-fuel-falsehoods-inclu/] , "regional water reservoirs in Southern California are at historic highs."
##
It is disheartening that so much disinformation is spreading during this crisis. The focus should be on fighting these fires and taking care of our first responders and victims.
The California Democratic Party stands ready to support those affected and to continue advocating for the necessary climate action to mitigate the underlying cause of these escalating climate disasters.
Our thoughts are with everyone in harm’s way.
— The whole team at CADEM HQ

clean_body: [] Dear friends, In times of crisis, the truth is more than ever. And unfortunately, social media makes it possible for lies to spread quicker than the speed of light. Here are some fact-checks to set the record straight. And you can always get up-to-date information from CaliforniaFireFacts.com [CaliforniaFireFacts.com] : CLAIM: California has cut the fire budget and personnel in recent years. FACT: The number of CalFIRE staff and the CalFIRE budget have nearly doubled since Gov. Newsom took office. CLAIM: These wildfires are caused by California’s mismanagement of forest lands. FACT: The budget for forest management is TEN TIMES larger than it was in 2018, and we have more than doubled the number of acres treated for wildfire resilience. Also, not all of the current fires even started in forested areas. CLAIM: California’s reservoirs are empty because all the water is "emptied out into the ocean.” FACT: Water reservoirs in Southern California are at record levels. There is no shortage of water in Southern California. PolitiFact independently found [] , "regional water reservoirs in Southern California are at historic highs." It is disheartening that so much disinformation is spreading during this crisis. The focus should be on fighting these fires and taking care of our first responders and victims. The California Democratic Party stands ready to support those affected and to continue advocating for the necessary climate action to mitigate the underlying cause of these escalating climate disasters. Our thoughts are with everyone in harm’s way. — The whole team at CADEM HQ DONATE » [] Our Democratic leaders are working hard to make California a better place to live. From fighting for good-paying jobs, combating climate change, to expanding healthcare access so all Californians can lead safe, healthy, prosperous lives — California’s Democratic leaders turn progressive ideas into meaningful action. name: VoteVets
subject: It’s a no from us
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS ACTION FUND
body:
Pete Hegseth sat in front of the Senate as he is considered for the role of Secretary of Defense, and VoteVets is going to be crystal clear about our position on his nomination:
#
Peter —
Pete Hegseth served. We’re grateful he answered the call. We honor that service.
But earlier this week, Pete Hegseth sat in front of the Senate as he is considered for the role of Secretary of Defense, and VoteVets is going to be crystal clear about our position on his nomination:
This guy has absolutely no place — none, zero, nada — commanding the finest Military in the history of mankind. Pete Hegseth is uniquely unqualified to lead the Army, Navy, Marines, Air Force, and Space Force. There is nothing on his resume that indicates he has what it takes to manage the largest and most complex federal agency in the United States — 3.4 million across our Active Duty, Reserves, Guard, and civilian contractors and employees.
It’s almost comical — but it’s so much worse than just that.
Lack of qualification is one thing, but Hegseth seems to want to impose a far-right extremist social engineering agenda on the United States Military. He has openly and publicly said that he wants to exclude women from combat roles after they have served valiantly in those roles for decades. He intends to restrict access to abortion for Active Duty and would do the same for Veterans. The list goes on.
The United States Military is the most effective and strongest fighting force the world has ever known because it harnesses the best people who can do the job from all corners of this nation. It doesn’t matter where your parents are from, who you love, which bathroom you use — the chief qualification is whether you can do the job. And our fighting men and women do the job better than anyone on the face of the earth. Bar none. To change that means you’re making our military weaker.
It’s gonna be a no from us, Pete. And if you agree, please:
[**Add your name and voice your opposition to Pete Hegseth as Secretary of Defense. We need to be loud and organized if we are going to successfully oppose this nomination.](https://act.votevets.org/signup/250113_vv_em_hegseth/?source=em250117-1-120&akid=34090%2E3013755%2EhjTuRr)**
| [ADD Your Name](https://act.votevets.org/signup/250113_vv_em_hegseth/?refcode=&akid=34090%2E3013755%2EhjTuRr)
---
Thank you,
The team at VoteVets

#
# **ICYMI: Protecting Worker Rights and Unions from Project 2025**
Last week, Senator Hughes had a [live discussion](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13262) with labor and economic experts about the threats to unions, labor laws, and worker rights that are outlined in Project 2025. Senator Hughes spoke with [Angela Ferritto](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13263), President at [AFL-CIO Pennsylvania](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13264), [Ryan Boyer](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13265), Business Manager at [Philadelphia Building and Construction Trades Council](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13266), and [David Cooper](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13267), Director of Economic Analysis at the [Economic Policy Institute](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13268). Together, they had a candid discussion about what worries them most about Project 2025 and why it's important for workers from all industries and trades to stay informed and engaged. [LISTEN OR WATCH THE DISCUSSION ONLINE](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13262)
* * *
**Key Takeaways** _Project 2025 seeks to:_
* Make it harder for workers to form a union
* Outlaw public sector unions
* Remove protections that prohibit retaliation against workers who engage in union organizing
* Change regulations to allow teenagers to work in dangerous occupations including minework and meatpacking
* Cut overtime pay and replace it with paid time off
* Privatize the administration of unemployment benefits

* * *
Overall, plans in Project 2025 seek to chip away at progress that has been made for all workers, not just union members, and put even more money in the pockets of millionaires and billionaires at the expense of the hard working people who power our economy. [As Angela Ferritto explained](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13262), those who are not union members will feel the worst impact of these changes because they do not have an organization who can stand up against this greed and push back against anti-worker policies. [](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13262) [WATCH HERE](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13262)
* * *
**Stay Engaged, Continue to Ask Questions** All of the panelists agreed that one of the best ways to prepare and fight back is to stay informed and engaged. We encourage you to listen or watch all the discussions Senator Hughes has been having on Project 2025's potential impacts on healthcare, social security, education, and workers. [All full conversations can be listened to or watched online.](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100169321.172456.176&gen=1&mailing_linkid=13262) As we all brace ourselves for the impacts the next Trump administration will have on the working class, Senator Hughes is working diligently to ensure that we are ready to respond at the state level whenever we can. State lawmakers have the ability to move forward a number of laws and investments to help hard working people. **Senator Hughes is ready to represent the interests of everyday people, not millionaires and billionaires.** Subscribe to our e-newsletter and follow us on social media to stay in the know about future webinars Senator Hughes will host about Project 2025. body:
Democrat Eric Swalwell represents California's 14th Congressional District.
https://ericswalwell.com [https://ericswalwell.com]
Friend,

We all know that Republicans are easily bought and sold – but it still pisses me off every time I see it in action. They don’t even pretend to represent working families anymore. Now, they answer to one guy only: Elon Musk.

I broke it all down on the I’ve Had It Podcast, and trust me, you don’t want to miss it. Click here to watch the full episode! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ESCA-14-Email-Jan2025-ENG-Podcast?&refcode=E12019-20250117-IveHadIt-SL-Other&amount=14]

SEE BEHIND THE SCENES » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/esca-14-email-Jan2025-ENG-Podcast?refcode=E12019-20250117-IveHadIt-SB-Other&amount=14]

The GOP has turned itself into Musk’s personal pit crew, bending over backwards to protect his billions while you struggle to keep up with rent, groceries and medical bills. Instead of working for the American people, they’re passing tax cuts for their ultra-wealthy buddies and doing Musk’s bidding in Congress.

Remember the bipartisan budget proposal that would fund childhood cancer research? Elon Musk twisted the GOP’s arm out of agreeing to it because it wasn’t ideal for the billionaires, regardless of how many Americans it would have helped.

And why? Because Musk’s money and influence are more valuable to them than your vote. That’s who they are, and that’s who they’ve always been.

If you’re just as outraged as I am and ready to hear the unfiltered truth about what happens behind the scenes on Capitol Hill, watch the episode now. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ESCA-14-Email-Jan2025-ENG-Podcast?&refcode=E12019-20250117-IveHadIt-SL-Other&amount=14]

WATCH THE EPISODE » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/esca-14-email-Jan2025-ENG-Podcast?refcode=E12019-20250117-IveHadIt-SB-Other&amount=14]

Let’s keep calling them out and fighting back.

— Eric

Friday, January 17, 2025 |
### MLK Day and lessons from his legacy
Join us January 20th at 8pm for our Monthly Statewide call. [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=MtBLw57MCBnd28lIl741u6P9-Hx0zs-QPm6VAaSuDh57pCpf-Mjr3dayMC0yHgY8LKPT4nZxN034OhzKGgT1zw&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2025_january_call_invite&n=2) Monday will be a day of reflection for a lot of us. It's a day to celebrate Martin Luther King Jr, it's also a day when we'll see a peaceful transition of power between two presidents with a long shared history of conflict. MLK lived in a time of stark divisions when American's couldn't seem to find a way to come together. We can see elements of that around us today. Hopefully we can remember Dr. King's example and find ways to work with people we disagree with to bring people together over shared values. This is different than abandoning your values just because it's easier to let the loudest voices in the room have their say. MLK spoke truth to power to gain support, but he also did the hard work behind the scenes to build a coalition. clean_body: Monday | | Friday, January 17, 2025 | MLK Day and lessons from his legacy Join us January 20th at 8pm for our Monthly Statewide call. Monday will be a day of reflection for a lot of us. It's a day to celebrate Martin Luther King Jr, it's also a day when we'll see a peaceful transition of power between two presidents with a long shared history of conflict. MLK lived in a time of stark divisions when American's couldn't seem to find a way to come together. We can see elements of that around us today. Hopefully we can remember Dr. King's example and find ways to work with people we disagree with to bring people together over shared values. This is different than abandoning your values just because it's easier to let the loudest voices in the room have their say. MLK spoke truth to power to gain support, but he also did the hard work behind the scenes to build a coalition. If you're unsatisfied with who is being inaugurated on Monday or the choices we were given, it's a great time to get working to improve a system that would lead to these results. U.S. Senator Katie Britt praised President-elect Donald Trump’s nominee for U.S. Attorney General during the confirmation hearing Wednesday.

Trump’s nominee Pam Bondi spoke and answered questions in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee about how she would lead the Justice Department in the new administration.

This was Britt’s first hearing as a part of the Judiciary Committee after being newly appointed to the committee.

The Food and Drug Administration announced on Wednesday that it is banning the use of Red Dye N0. 3 in all foods produced in America. The organization has come under fire recently from legislators on both sides of the aisle for allowing the dye’s continued use in foods despite studies indicating it contains possible carcinogens and could have detrimental effects on neurological development.

“The FDA is taking action that will remove the authorization for the use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food and ingested drugs,” said Jim Jones, the FDA’s deputy commissioner for human foods. “Evidence shows cancer in laboratory male rats exposed to high levels of FD&C Red No.3. Importantly, the way that FD&C Red No. 3 causes cancer in male rats does not occur in humans.”

Leading the charge against the use of harmful dyes in foods are Senators Tommy Tuberville and Katie Britt. Both elected officials have expressed the importance of reevaluating the use of dyes in foods, with both calling for the total ban of Red No. 3 and Red 40. Officials with the FDA recently said that Red 40 hasn’t been evaluated in more than a decade.

clean_body: | Welcome to the Indiana Democratic Party's weekly newsletter, The Kernel of Truth. The State Party will provide the most important fact - a kernel of truth - from the week. ** Democrats Push Back on Dangerous Republican Budget Proposals With the 2025 legislative session underway, the Republican supermajority is trying to force through several changes to the next budget that threaten the healthcare coverage for thousands of Hoosiers and would force major cuts for many public schools. School districts would lose hundreds of million in funding, all while wealthy households would be eligible for vouchers, pulling even more dollars away from local public schools. It’s dangerous, and Democrats are fighting to stop this backward agenda. Republican Supermajority Proposes Over a Billion Dollars in Annual Cuts for Schools and Local Governments The Republican supermajority announced their proposed changes to the property tax system, and the results would be disastrous for schools and local governments while providing little to no relief for families. The average household would save just around $200 per year on their property tax bill, but many middle class households wouldn’t save a cent. In return, schools lose hundreds of millions of dollars and police and public safety budgets will have to be slashed in towns, cities, and counties across Indiana. Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks. Senate Democrats launched their legislative agenda this week, and it includes focusing on infant and maternal healthcare, affordable housing, and protecting Indiana’s public schools. State Senate Minority Leader Shelli Yoder also laid out her vision for expanded environmental protections for wild areas, and the importance of making this session about working Hoosiers, not special interests. Get Involved! Opportunities After the Election As we move past the 2024 Election, it is imperative that we unite together to create a better future for our state. One of the best ways to do that is to help us rebuild our party and grow in the coming months and years. Make Your Voice Heard! A new Congress has begun. Soon, Donald Trump will be sworn in as our next president. If history is any guide, Trump and his allies will spend their first few weeks in office pushing disastrous policy after disastrous policy. * * *
It's January 17th, 2025. Happy New Year.

I take heart from the example of the Native Americans, who suffered five centuries of genocide, displacement, extermination, cultural erasure, bias, and persecution - and still kept their songs, traditions, and culture alive. Even in secret. Even as their social fabric was attacked and severely damaged, almost destroyed. Even as their children were stolen, their ceremonies outlawed, their languages criminalized. They kept going. They remembered their prophecies. They refused to lose sight of their culture. Everyone? No. Countless people lost their lives, their minds, their families, their memories, in travesties and tragedies big enough for the whole world to grieve, like many others. But enough people survived, supported each other, and invested their lives in the work of carrying their wisdom forward, that we see a resurgence of the beauty and vitality of their cultures today - which greatly increases the odds that our shared future will be better than our past. Praise be.
This is not a comfortable way to look at life. But it's an honest one. And truth be told, we are not living in comfortable times.
Once, fifteen years ago, I was a participant at a "Transition Town" training, organized to teach local folks how to start "Transition Town" groups in their neighborhood. (The idea was that waiting for the government or corporations to take major steps to prevent future disasters was a vain hope - but there's a great deal that local folks can do in community to increase our resilience and reduce the energy intensity of our lifestyles, while improving our health, culture, and social fabric.) The training opened with an assessment of four possible pathways into humanity's future:
1. Catastrophic population collapse, driven by climate disaster, supply chain disruption, new pathogens, and/or genocide.
2. Moderate population decline, then stabilization: humanity faces some losses, but collectively we strengthen our resilience on this shared planet and arrive at a reasonable "carrying capacity" on Earth.
3. A continued, gradual increase in population that levels off not much higher than it is today, as efforts at sustainability and resilience pay off and we collectively invest in protecting and supporting one another.
4. Continued population growth: our rapid innovation in technology is able to overcome our environmental crises, and we continue to reproduce and increase our numbers as a species essentially without limit.

The organizers gave us a moment to consider which we personally thought most likely - which mapped well onto the emotional states (and, to a substantial degree, the economic level) of people in the room, as you might expect. Then they gave us the twist: **all** of those outcomes can - and probably will - happen simultaneously. Depending where you are on the planet - what your race, country of origin, economic position, gender, personal traits, and simple luck turn out to be - _each_ of those outcomes will be experienced by some people, somewhere, on Earth over the next few decades.
Leading to the direct question - what can we do in our own lives to increase the odds of surviving, even thriving, through these times, while helping others to do the same?

When I get to thinking in these directions, the floodgates open. This is what I spent fifteen years of my life studying. I knew from late childhood, thanks to my father's career and his investment in mentoring me, that the 21st century was going to bring immense changes - environmental destruction, geopolitical conflict, mass migration, rising nationalism and tyranny, economic...transitions, to put it mildly. So I decided at the age of 16 to invest my energies into learning everything it would take - politically, socially, environmentally, economically - to design and create healthy **systems** of a sustainable human civilization on planet Earth. I learned a LOT. And there's **so much** I have to share.
It's tough to translate that into politics, to be honest. It's not the simplistic sort of message that packs well into a TV ad, and it doesn't align with the economic interests that drive most of our successful politicians these days. So I feel torn. On the one hand, achieving a decision-making position, with 1. the direct power to effect change, and 2. the larger platform to spread important messages, carries real and important benefits and the capacity to serve, protect, and reach people in a larger way. On the other hand, the self-censorship required, the _massive_ effort, the cyclical nature of campaigning, the susceptibility to attack, and the uncertainty of the result create a large opportunity cost. Could I more effectively and peacefully grow my impact and influence, spread helpful knowledge, and beneficially affect more people, through another approach? This question occurs in the context that I have two children under the age of two, and a beloved caregiver and a husband in a wheelchair who are aging and whose long-term health is uncertain. It also occurs in the context that running the campaign cost our family - dearly - in so many dimensions.
I share this vulnerably, in the hope of being understood, and I'd love to know your thoughts.

We have a ceasefire agreement, for now. Alhamdulillah - may it bring peace to the suffering. But ceasefire is not the end of apartheid - nor is it the end of the war machine that generates genocide for profits. The end of that war machine's influence in American politics? The influence of foreign lobbies in US domestic lawmaking in particular? More work remains to be done. The cause of Palestine is and will remain the cause of free people everywhere. As I said last April, "we have to elect good people for America; we have to **change the world** for Peace and opportunity for all."
I just wonder - is the political forum the most effective place for _me_ to fight that fight? And is now the right time?
Changing the world so that genocide (anywhere) is no longer an option, is a long-term and systems-level journey. Systems change is never linear. It's incremental and indirect, right up until it is openly and rapidly - sometimes cataclysmically - transformative. It's a conversation here, a small effort there (and a big one that seems initially fruitless somewhere else...), consistently and persistently, knowing that the changes we seek almost never come on a timeline we can foretell. It's investing in future generations, educating for change, connecting with our neighbors, having the conversations we're nervous about, trusting ourselves and each other enough to tell the truth. It's believing that we are not special, but all are important. It's putting principle before self-interest, and loving for our neighbor what we love for ourselves. It's knowing in our bones that we are just as capable as our ancestors - and it's understanding that we are duty-bound to do everything we can to leave a better world for our children.

In the meantime, Washington has a new Governor and slate of executives, several new legislators (congratulations to Osman Salahuddin, Tina Orwall, Vandana Slatter, Edwin Obras, and others I've had the great pleasure of getting to know). There is nowhere else in the United States where I'd feel safer, as the Muslim, immigrant, mixed-race, mixed-status, mixed-ability family that I'm in, and I'm glad, and cautiously optimistic about our future in this beautiful place that we call home.
One thing is certain - we are all in for a heck of a time. I encourage us - I encourage you - invest in building trust with your neighbors. Invest in strengthening your local supply chains and reducing your overall cost of living. Learn how to fix your car, your water heater, your plumbing, your leaky roof. Get better at first aid, medical care, and skills to support your family's health (cooking, nutrition, exercise, herbal medicine, etc). Get to know your kids' friends. Diversify your income streams and your financial life as much as possible. Get a passport, and to really know folks near and far - you will be amazed at your family's personal growth and how much one can learn and understand better. Reduce your vulnerability to sudden shocks - like a job loss, car breakdown, or economic crisis. This will also increase your breathing room to speak up or make change in the ways that are available to you, with less fear - and we all need you, and you need every one of us, to speak up and make change, and to be resilient enough to be a resource more than a burden, whatever the future holds.
Protect one another. Care for one another. Value yourself, value the world around you, and let's see this through, together.

On the other hand, the self-censorship required, the massive effort, the cyclical nature of campaigning, the susceptibility to attack, and the uncertainty of the result create a large opportunity cost. Could I more effectively and peacefully grow my impact and influence, spread helpful knowledge, and beneficially affect more people, through another approach? This question occurs in the context that I have two children under the age of two, and a beloved caregiver and a husband in a wheelchair who are aging and whose long-term health is uncertain. It also occurs in the context that running the campaign cost our family - dearly - in so many dimensions. I share this vulnerably, in the hope of being understood, and I'd love to know your thoughts. We have a ceasefire agreement, for now. Alhamdulillah - may it bring peace to the suffering. Even as Blinken refuses to answer questions and has journalists and casually acknowledges that Israel utterly failed in its goal of eradicating, or even weakening, Hamas; even as Biden takes to Twitter to claim that the ceasefire was only reached "because of the pressure Israel built on Hamas, backed by the United States" nauseatingly justifying the genocide right to his final day in office. But ceasefire is not the end of apartheid - nor is it the end of the war machine that generates genocide for profits. The end of that war machine's influence in American politics? The influence of foreign lobbies in US domestic lawmaking in particular? More work remains to be done. The cause of Palestine is and will remain the cause of free people everywhere. As I said last April, "we have to elect good people for America; we have to change the world** for Peace and opportunity for all." I just wonder - is the political forum the most effective place for me to fight that fight? And is now the right time? Changing the world so that genocide (anywhere) is no longer an option, is a long-term and systems-level journey. Systems change is never linear. It's incremental and indirect, right up until it is openly and rapidly - sometimes cataclysmically - transformative. It's a conversation here, a small effort there (and a big one that seems initially fruitless somewhere else...), consistently and persistently, knowing that the changes we seek almost never come on a timeline we can foretell. It's investing in future generations, educating for change, connecting with our neighbors, having the conversations we're nervous about, trusting ourselves and each other enough to tell the truth. It's believing that we are not special, but all are important. It's putting principle before self-interest, and loving for our neighbor what we love for ourselves. It's knowing in our bones that we are just as capable as our ancestors - and it's understanding that we are duty-bound to do everything we can to leave a better world for our children. In the meantime, Washington has a new Governor and slate of executives, several new legislators (congratulations to Osman Salahuddin, Tina Orwall, Vandana Slatter, Edwin Obras, and others I've had the great pleasure of getting to know). There is nowhere else in the United States where I'd feel safer, as the Muslim, immigrant, mixed-race, mixed-status, mixed-ability family that I'm in, and I'm glad, and cautiously optimistic about our future in this beautiful place that we call home. One thing is certain - we are all in for a heck of a time. I encourage us - I encourage you - invest in building trust with your neighbors. Invest in strengthening your local supply chains and reducing your overall cost of living. Learn how to fix your car, your water heater, your plumbing, your leaky roof. Get better at first aid, medical care, and skills to support your family's health (cooking, nutrition, exercise, herbal medicine, etc). Get to know your kids' friends. Diversify your income streams and your financial life as much as possible. Get a passport, and to really know folks near and far - you will be amazed at your family's personal growth and how much one can learn and understand better. Reduce your vulnerability to sudden shocks - like a job loss, car breakdown, or economic crisis. This will also increase your breathing room to speak up or make change in the ways that are available to you, with less fear - and we all need you, and you need every one of us, to speak up and make change, and to be resilient enough to be a resource more than a burden, whatever the future holds. Protect one another. Care for one another. Value yourself, value the world around you, and let's see this through, together. ?
